subject: astronomy
title: Cosmology Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Tie expansion, dark matter and dark energy together in exam-style answers.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy stretch: dark matter, dark energy and exam-style cosmology.
final_note: Most of the universe is invisible — but its effects are everywhere.

concepts.def: Invisible mass detected only by its gravity.
Light elements formed minutes after the Big Bang.
Stars at galaxy edge move too fast for visible mass alone.
Discovered 1998 from distant Type Ia supernovae.
Discovered the CMB in 1965 as background hiss.

walkthroughs.body_html: Stars at the outer edge of spiral galaxies orbit far faster than visible mass alone would allow. Either gravity behaves differently or there is extra invisible mass — dark matter. It outweighs normal matter ~5:1.
In 1998, observations of Type Ia supernovae showed expansion is accelerating. The cause, called dark energy, makes up ~68% of the universe's content.
For 'evidence for Big Bang' answers: state Hubble's redshift law, the CMB at 2.7 K, and the cosmic abundance of hydrogen/helium from nucleosynthesis. Each piece is independent supporting evidence.

numericals.q: Approximately what percentage of the universe is dark energy?
